items.title: A local ring map with finite residue extension admits a prime outside the closed fibre whose quotient is quasi-finite over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a local map of local rings A -> B, essentially of finite type with A Noetherian and the residue field extension finite, any open V of Spec B containing a prime not lying over the closed point of A contains a prime q, not meeting the closed point of A, such that A -> B/q is a localization of a quasi-finite ring map. The retained proof is written: B is Noetherian; the punctured spectrum of B is Jacobson (Properties, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson) so a closed point q can be chosen inside the nonempty open cut out from V by removing primes over m_A; the two-point spectrum of B/q plus the isolated-point criterion (Algebra, lemma-isolated-point-fibre) show finite type A-algebra C presenting B/q is quasi-finite at the corresponding prime, and Zariski's open locus for quasi-finiteness (Algebra, lemma-quasi-finite-open) finishes after a principal localization. Retained author proof at lines 14969-14991.
